paragraphs.title: Preparing the Plot and the Brothers’ Departure

easy.question: What did Joseph command to be put in the men’s sacks?
answers: Food
Clothes
Tools
easy.explanation: Joseph commanded that the men’s sacks be filled with food.

easy.question: What was to be placed in the mouth of each man’s sack?
answers: Bread
Money
A cup
easy.explanation: Joseph commanded that each man’s money be put in the mouth of his sack.

easy.question: Who set out with the men in the morning?
answers: Joseph
The members of his household
Their donkeys
easy.explanation: The men were sent away together with their donkeys.

medium.question: What did Joseph’s steward do after receiving his instructions?
answers: He did exactly as Joseph said
He brought the men back to Egypt
He took their donkeys
medium.explanation: The verse says that he did according to Joseph’s word.

medium.question: What additional object was put in the youngest brother’s sack?
answers: A sword
A silver cup
A garment
medium.explanation: The silver cup was placed in the youngest brother’s sack.

medium.question: In the phrase “as much as they can carry,” what does it mean?
answers: As much as they can sleep
As much as they can drink
As much as they can carry
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the amount of food the men could carry in their sacks.

challenge.question: What was unusual about the youngest brother’s sack?
answers: It contained both the cup and his money
It contained no food
It was left in Joseph’s house
challenge.explanation: The silver cup and the youngest brother’s money were both placed in his sack.

challenge.question: What does “As soon as the morning was light” indicate about their departure?
answers: They left at night
They left at daybreak
They left at noon
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that they set out at the beginning of the day.

challenge.question: Why does the verse add “they and their donkeys”?
answers: To say that the donkeys stayed in Egypt
To show that the donkeys belonged to Joseph
To make clear that both the men and their donkeys left
challenge.explanation: The wording emphasizes that the men departed together with their donkeys.

questions.question: What was unusual about the youngest brother’s sack?
answers: It contained both the cup and his money
It contained no food
It was left in Joseph’s house
questions.explanation: The silver cup and the youngest brother’s money were both placed in his sack.

questions.question: What does “As soon as the morning was light” indicate about their departure?
answers: They left at night
They left at daybreak
They left at noon
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that they set out at the beginning of the day.

questions.question: Why does the verse add “they and their donkeys”?
answers: To say that the donkeys stayed in Egypt
To show that the donkeys belonged to Joseph
To make clear that both the men and their donkeys left
questions.explanation: The wording emphasizes that the men departed together with their donkeys.

easy.question: Who commanded that the men be pursued?
answers: Joseph
Pharaoh
Judah
easy.explanation: Joseph told his steward to get up and pursue the men.

easy.question: What did the brothers do when the pursuit began?
answers: They entered the city
They went out of the city
They returned to Joseph’s house
easy.explanation: The brothers had gone out of the city, though they were not yet far away.

easy.question: What did Joseph’s steward do after overtaking the men?
answers: He took them to the king’s house
He brought them back to the city
He spoke these words to them
easy.explanation: After overtaking them, he spoke the words Joseph had commanded.

medium.question: Why was the steward sent to pursue the brothers?
answers: To accuse them of repaying good with evil
To invite them to a feast
To give them gifts
medium.explanation: He was told to ask why they had rewarded evil for good.

medium.question: What does the accusation that Joseph used the cup to divine mean in context?
answers: The cup was made of gold
Joseph supposedly used the cup to discover hidden things
The cup belonged to one of the brothers
medium.explanation: The cup is presented as a special object through which Joseph supposedly practiced divination.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: The steward overtook them, they left the city, and Joseph ordered the pursuit
Joseph ordered the pursuit, the brothers returned, and the steward drank from the cup
The brothers left without going far, Joseph ordered the pursuit, and the steward overtook them
medium.explanation: The brothers left the city, Joseph ordered the pursuit, and the steward then caught them.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “not yet far off”?
answers: The brothers could be caught quickly
The brothers had not left the city
The brothers had already reached Joseph’s house
challenge.explanation: Because they were still nearby, the steward was able to overtake them quickly.

challenge.question: Why does the accusation “you have done evil” fit Joseph’s claim?
answers: The brothers were late to the feast
They were accused of repaying good with evil
They refused to drink from the cup
challenge.explanation: The accusation connects their supposed theft with the charge that they repaid good with evil.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by the words “Is not this it”?
answers: That the cup was already broken
That the brothers wanted to buy the cup
That this was Joseph’s special cup
challenge.explanation: The words identify the cup as Joseph’s important and distinctive possession.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “not yet far off”?
answers: The brothers could be caught quickly
The brothers had not left the city
The brothers had already reached Joseph’s house
questions.explanation: Because they were still nearby, the steward was able to overtake them quickly.

questions.question: Why does the accusation “you have done evil” fit Joseph’s claim?
answers: The brothers were late to the feast
They were accused of repaying good with evil
They refused to drink from the cup
questions.explanation: The accusation connects their supposed theft with the charge that they repaid good with evil.

questions.question: What is emphasized by the words “Is not this it”?
answers: That the cup was already broken
That the brothers wanted to buy the cup
That this was Joseph’s special cup
questions.explanation: The words identify the cup as Joseph’s important and distinctive possession.

paragraphs.title: The Brothers’ Protest and Their Proposed Punishment

easy.question: What did the brothers deny stealing from their lord’s house?
answers: Silver or gold
Food from Egypt
Their father’s property
easy.explanation: They said it was impossible for them to steal silver or gold from their lord’s house.

easy.question: What had the brothers done with the money found in their sacks?
answers: They kept it
They brought it back to Egypt
They gave it to their father
easy.explanation: They reminded the steward that they had brought the money back to Egypt.

easy.question: What punishment did the brothers propose for whoever had the stolen object?
answers: He should be sent to Canaan
He should surrender his money
He should die, and all the brothers should become slaves
easy.explanation: They proposed that the guilty man die and that all of them become their lord’s slaves.

medium.question: How did the brothers argue that theft was unlikely?
answers: They had already returned money found in their sacks
They were soldiers
They had never entered the lord’s house
medium.explanation: They argued that people who returned found money would not steal silver or gold.

medium.question: What does the phrase “God forbid” express in this context?
answers: Certainly yes
Absolutely not
Perhaps later
medium.explanation: The phrase strongly rejects the possibility that they would commit such an act.

medium.question: What was the difference between the brothers’ proposal and the steward’s response?
answers: The brothers asked that everyone be freed
The brothers proposed punishment for all, but the steward said only the guilty man would be a slave
The steward demanded that everyone die
medium.explanation: The brothers proposed death for the guilty man and slavery for all, while the steward limited slavery to the guilty man.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the brothers’ offer, “we also will be my lord’s bondmen”?
answers: They were willing to share responsibility for the situation
They wanted to remain in Egypt voluntarily
They did not trust their brother
challenge.explanation: They offered to suffer together if the stolen object was found.

challenge.question: Why did the brothers specifically mention “silver or gold”?
answers: To request additional payment
To emphasize that they would not steal valuables from their lord’s house
To explain why they had gone to Canaan
challenge.explanation: Mentioning silver and gold strengthens their claim that they would not steal valuable objects.

challenge.question: What important detail changed between the brothers’ words and the steward’s answer?
answers: The brothers mentioned silver, while the steward mentioned gold
The brothers spoke to Pharaoh, while the steward spoke to Jacob
The brothers proposed death and slavery for all, while the steward required slavery only for the guilty man
challenge.explanation: The steward softened their proposed punishment by limiting slavery to the person with the cup.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the brothers’ offer, “we also will be my lord’s bondmen”?
answers: They were willing to share responsibility for the situation
They wanted to remain in Egypt voluntarily
They did not trust their brother
questions.explanation: They offered to suffer together if the stolen object was found.

questions.question: Why did the brothers specifically mention “silver or gold”?
answers: To request additional payment
To emphasize that they would not steal valuables from their lord’s house
To explain why they had gone to Canaan
questions.explanation: Mentioning silver and gold strengthens their claim that they would not steal valuable objects.

questions.question: What important detail changed between the brothers’ words and the steward’s answer?
answers: The brothers mentioned silver, while the steward mentioned gold
The brothers spoke to Pharaoh, while the steward spoke to Jacob
The brothers proposed death and slavery for all, while the steward required slavery only for the guilty man
questions.explanation: The steward softened their proposed punishment by limiting slavery to the person with the cup.

paragraphs.title: The Search and the Cup in Benjamin’s Sack

easy.question: What was found in Benjamin’s sack?
answers: The cup
Money
Bread
easy.explanation: The cup was found in Benjamin’s sack.

easy.question: What did the brothers do at the beginning of the search?
answers: They returned to the city
They lowered their sacks and opened them
They tore their clothes
easy.explanation: Each man quickly lowered his sack to the ground and opened it.

easy.question: What did the brothers do after the cup was found?
answers: They continued on their way
They rejoiced
They tore their clothes
easy.explanation: They tore their clothes as an expression of grief and distress.

medium.question: In what order were the sacks searched?
answers: From the oldest to the youngest
From the youngest to the oldest
All at the same time
medium.explanation: The search began with the oldest and ended with the youngest.

medium.question: What is a sack in the phrase “each man lowered his sack”?
answers: A garment
A bag or pack
A donkey
medium.explanation: The men lowered and opened the bags in which they carried their belongings.

medium.question: Why did the brothers have to return to the city?
answers: They had run out of food
They wanted to meet Joseph
The cup had been found in Benjamin’s sack
medium.explanation: After the cup was found with Benjamin, they tore their clothes and returned to the city.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the brothers’ tearing their clothes?
answers: They were in great distress
They were preparing for a celebration
They wanted to change clothes
challenge.explanation: Tearing one’s clothes was an expression of mourning, grief, and distress.

challenge.question: What does “each man” emphasize in “each man lowered his sack”?
answers: Only one man opened his sack
Every brother opened his own sack
Only Benjamin opened his sack
challenge.explanation: The wording shows that every brother opened his own sack.

challenge.question: What detail creates suspense during the search?
answers: The brothers searched only Benjamin’s sack
They returned to the city before searching
The search moved from the oldest brother to the youngest, and the cup was found only at the end
challenge.explanation: The cup’s discovery in Benjamin’s sack is delayed until the final search.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the brothers’ tearing their clothes?
answers: They were in great distress
They were preparing for a celebration
They wanted to change clothes
questions.explanation: Tearing one’s clothes was an expression of mourning, grief, and distress.

questions.question: What does “each man” emphasize in “each man lowered his sack”?
answers: Only one man opened his sack
Every brother opened his own sack
Only Benjamin opened his sack
questions.explanation: The wording shows that every brother opened his own sack.

questions.question: What detail creates suspense during the search?
answers: The brothers searched only Benjamin’s sack
They returned to the city before searching
The search moved from the oldest brother to the youngest, and the cup was found only at the end
questions.explanation: The cup’s discovery in Benjamin’s sack is delayed until the final search.

paragraphs.title: The Brothers Before Joseph and the Sentence

easy.question: Who came to Joseph’s house?
answers: Judah and his brothers
Jacob and his sons
Pharaoh and his servants
easy.explanation: Judah and his brothers came to Joseph’s house.

easy.question: What did Judah and his brothers do before Joseph?
answers: They stood at the gate
They fell to the ground before him
They went out to their father
easy.explanation: They fell before Joseph on the ground.

easy.question: What deed did Joseph ask the brothers about?
answers: Selling grain
Leaving their father
The cup found with one of them
easy.explanation: Joseph asked what they had done after the cup was found with one of them.

medium.question: What did Judah propose after the cup was found?
answers: That all of them become Joseph’s slaves
That only Benjamin become a slave
That they return immediately to their father
medium.explanation: Judah said that all of them, including the one with the cup, would be Joseph’s servants.

medium.question: What does “how shall we clear ourselves?” mean in context?
answers: How can we prove that we are innocent?
How can we set out?
How can we ask for food?
medium.explanation: Judah asks how they can defend themselves and prove their innocence.

medium.question: What was the difference between Judah’s proposal and Joseph’s response?
answers: Judah wanted everyone to be slaves, and Joseph agreed
Judah wanted everyone to be slaves, but Joseph required only the one with the cup to remain
Judah wanted the cup’s owner to remain, but Joseph required everyone to remain
medium.explanation: Joseph said that only the man with the cup would be his servant.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Judah’s words, “God hath found out the iniquity of thy servants”?
answers: Judah thought everything happened by chance
Judah saw the situation as the exposure or punishment of sin
Judah believed Joseph had stolen the cup
challenge.explanation: Judah says that God has brought their guilt to light.

challenge.question: What does Joseph emphasize by saying “the man in whose hand the cup is found”?
answers: The punishment will fall on the man with the cup
The cup belongs to all the brothers
None of the brothers will be punished
challenge.explanation: Joseph distinguishes the cup’s owner from the other brothers and assigns the punishment to him.

challenge.question: What does “get you up in peace unto your father” mean in this situation?
answers: All the brothers must remain in Egypt
The brothers without the cup may return to their father
The brothers must take Joseph to their father
challenge.explanation: Joseph tells the other brothers to return safely to their father.

questions.question: What can be inferred from Judah’s words, “God hath found out the iniquity of thy servants”?
answers: Judah thought everything happened by chance
Judah saw the situation as the exposure or punishment of sin
Judah believed Joseph had stolen the cup
questions.explanation: Judah says that God has brought their guilt to light.

questions.question: What does Joseph emphasize by saying “the man in whose hand the cup is found”?
answers: The punishment will fall on the man with the cup
The cup belongs to all the brothers
None of the brothers will be punished
questions.explanation: Joseph distinguishes the cup’s owner from the other brothers and assigns the punishment to him.

questions.question: What does “get you up in peace unto your father” mean in this situation?
answers: All the brothers must remain in Egypt
The brothers without the cup may return to their father
The brothers must take Joseph to their father
questions.explanation: Joseph tells the other brothers to return safely to their father.

paragraphs.title: Judah Approaches and Asks to Be Heard

easy.question: Who approached the ruler and spoke to him?
answers: Judah
Joseph
Benjamin
easy.explanation: Judah approached Joseph and spoke to him.

easy.question: What did the ruler ask the brothers?
answers: Whether they had money
Whether they had a father or brother
Whether they knew Pharaoh
easy.explanation: The ruler asked whether they had a father or a brother.

easy.question: What did the brothers say about the younger brother?
answers: He remained in Canaan
He was sent alone to Egypt
He was his mother’s only remaining child and his father loved him
easy.explanation: They said that the younger son was the only one left of his mother and that his father loved him.

medium.question: Why did Judah ask the ruler not to be angry with him?
answers: He wanted to leave immediately
He was about to speak and make an important request
He had forgotten the ruler’s name
medium.explanation: Judah asked permission to speak and requested that the ruler not become angry.

medium.question: What is the order of events in these verses?
answers: The ruler asked a question, and the brothers told him about their father and brother
The brothers described their father, and then the ruler asked about their brother
Judah left his brothers and then arrived in Egypt
medium.explanation: The ruler first asked whether they had a father or brother, and the brothers then answered.

medium.question: What does “speak a word in my lord’s ears” mean?
answers: Speak loudly before everyone
Write secretly
Speak personally and directly to him
medium.explanation: The phrase means that Judah wants to address the ruler directly.

challenge.question: What did Judah emphasize by saying “thou art even as Pharaoh”?
answers: The ruler had authority nearly equal to Pharaoh’s
The ruler was actually Pharaoh
The ruler was Pharaoh’s father
challenge.explanation: Judah compared the ruler’s authority with Pharaoh’s; he did not say they were the same person.

challenge.question: Why did the brothers mention that one brother was dead and Benjamin remained alone to his mother?
answers: To prove that they knew the names of all Egyptians
To emphasize their family situation and arouse compassion
To say that they did not know their father
challenge.explanation: These details strengthened Judah’s appeal and highlighted the family’s distress.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “a child of his old age” and the statement that his father loved him?
answers: Benjamin was the oldest son
Benjamin was a child his father did not know
Benjamin was his father’s youngest son and especially precious to him
challenge.explanation: The description identifies Benjamin as the child born in his father’s old age and especially loved by him.

questions.question: What did Judah emphasize by saying “thou art even as Pharaoh”?
answers: The ruler had authority nearly equal to Pharaoh’s
The ruler was actually Pharaoh
The ruler was Pharaoh’s father
questions.explanation: Judah compared the ruler’s authority with Pharaoh’s; he did not say they were the same person.

questions.question: Why did the brothers mention that one brother was dead and Benjamin remained alone to his mother?
answers: To prove that they knew the names of all Egyptians
To emphasize their family situation and arouse compassion
To say that they did not know their father
questions.explanation: These details strengthened Judah’s appeal and highlighted the family’s distress.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “a child of his old age” and the statement that his father loved him?
answers: Benjamin was the oldest son
Benjamin was a child his father did not know
Benjamin was his father’s youngest son and especially precious to him
questions.explanation: The description identifies Benjamin as the child born in his father’s old age and especially loved by him.

easy.question: Whom did the ruler ask the brothers to bring to him?
answers: Their youngest brother
Their father
One of his servants
easy.explanation: The ruler asked them to bring their youngest brother to him.

easy.question: What did the brothers say about the boy?
answers: He wanted to leave his father
He could not leave his father
He did not know his father
easy.explanation: They said that the boy could not leave his father.

easy.question: What would happen if the younger brother did not come with them?
answers: The brothers would return home immediately
The ruler would send him elsewhere
The brothers would not see the ruler’s face again
easy.explanation: The ruler warned that they would not see his face again unless their brother came.

medium.question: Why were the brothers afraid to take the boy from his father?
answers: His leaving could cause his father’s death
The boy did not want to go to Egypt
The ruler forbade them to speak with him
medium.explanation: They said that if the boy left his father, his father would die.

medium.question: What does “Bring him down unto me” mean in context?
answers: Hide him
Bring him to the ruler
Return him to his father
medium.explanation: The ruler was asking them to bring the boy to him in Egypt.

medium.question: What sequence of events is described?
answers: The ruler requested the boy, the brothers explained their concern, and the ruler stated a condition
The brothers brought the boy, the ruler freed them, and they returned
The father asked to see the ruler, and the boy remained alone
medium.explanation: The ruler made the request, the brothers explained their father’s dependence on the boy, and the ruler gave his condition.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “that I may set mine eyes upon him”?
answers: The ruler wanted to watch over and care for the boy
The ruler wanted to punish him immediately
The ruler wanted to hide him from everyone
challenge.explanation: The expression suggests paying close attention to someone and watching over him.

challenge.question: What does the brothers’ response show about the relationship between the boy and his father?
answers: The boy was his father’s only child
The boy was extremely dear to his father, and losing him could endanger the father
The boy feared his brothers more than his father
challenge.explanation: They emphasized that the father could die if the boy left him, showing how precious the boy was.

challenge.question: Why did the condition “ye shall see my face no more” put pressure on the brothers?
answers: They would lose access to the ruler’s food and help
They would have to remain in the city
They would lose the chance to meet the ruler and ask for further help
challenge.explanation: Without the younger brother, they could not return to the ruler or seek his assistance.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “that I may set mine eyes upon him”?
answers: The ruler wanted to watch over and care for the boy
The ruler wanted to punish him immediately
The ruler wanted to hide him from everyone
questions.explanation: The expression suggests paying close attention to someone and watching over him.

questions.question: What does the brothers’ response show about the relationship between the boy and his father?
answers: The boy was his father’s only child
The boy was extremely dear to his father, and losing him could endanger the father
The boy feared his brothers more than his father
questions.explanation: They emphasized that the father could die if the boy left him, showing how precious the boy was.

questions.question: Why did the condition “ye shall see my face no more” put pressure on the brothers?
answers: They would lose access to the ruler’s food and help
They would have to remain in the city
They would lose the chance to meet the ruler and ask for further help
questions.explanation: Without the younger brother, they could not return to the ruler or seek his assistance.

paragraphs.title: Jacob Fears Losing Benjamin as Well

easy.question: To whom did the brothers go and report the ruler’s words?
answers: Their father
Pharaoh
Benjamin
easy.explanation: The brothers went to their father and told him what the ruler had said.

easy.question: What did their father tell his sons to do?
answers: Return to Egypt without Benjamin
Return and buy a little food
Stay at home
easy.explanation: Their father told them to return and buy a little food.

easy.question: Why did the brothers say they could not go down to Egypt without their younger brother?
answers: They had no money
The journey was dangerous
They could not see the ruler’s face without their brother
easy.explanation: They said they could not see the man’s face unless their youngest brother was with them.

medium.question: What did the brothers do after telling their father the ruler’s words?
answers: They explained that they had to take their younger brother
They immediately returned to Egypt
They returned all the food
medium.explanation: They explained that they could go down only if their younger brother went with them.

medium.question: What does “buy us a little food” mean in context?
answers: Break food into pieces
Purchase or obtain food
Set food aside
medium.explanation: Here the expression means to buy or obtain food, not to break it.

medium.question: What can be understood from the father’s words about his sons and the missing son?
answers: He did not remember his sons
The younger son had already returned
He feared losing the younger son as well
medium.explanation: Because one son had already disappeared, Jacob feared that something would happen to Benjamin too.

challenge.question: What did Jacob mean by “ye shall bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to the grave”?
answers: If Benjamin suffered, Jacob’s grief could bring about his death
Jacob wanted to go down to Egypt himself
Jacob wanted Benjamin buried in Egypt
challenge.explanation: Jacob described the depth of his grief, saying it could bring him to death.

challenge.question: Why did the brothers mention that one son had gone out and never been seen again?
answers: To explain where he lived
To explain why Jacob feared sending the younger son too
To prove that the ruler had lied
challenge.explanation: The disappearance of the first son explains Jacob’s great fear for Benjamin.

challenge.question: Who do “the one” and “this also” refer to in Jacob’s words?
answers: “The one” is Benjamin, and “this” is Judah
“The one” is Reuben, and “this” is Simeon
“The one” is the missing son, and “this” is the younger son
challenge.explanation: “The one” refers to the son who disappeared, while “this also” refers to Benjamin.

questions.question: What did Jacob mean by “ye shall bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to the grave”?
answers: If Benjamin suffered, Jacob’s grief could bring about his death
Jacob wanted to go down to Egypt himself
Jacob wanted Benjamin buried in Egypt
questions.explanation: Jacob described the depth of his grief, saying it could bring him to death.

questions.question: Why did the brothers mention that one son had gone out and never been seen again?
answers: To explain where he lived
To explain why Jacob feared sending the younger son too
To prove that the ruler had lied
questions.explanation: The disappearance of the first son explains Jacob’s great fear for Benjamin.

questions.question: Who do “the one” and “this also” refer to in Jacob’s words?
answers: “The one” is Benjamin, and “this” is Judah
“The one” is Reuben, and “this” is Simeon
“The one” is the missing son, and “this” is the younger son
questions.explanation: “The one” refers to the son who disappeared, while “this also” refers to Benjamin.

Pharaoh
His brothers
easy.explanation: Judah said that he would return to his father.

easy.question: Who would not be with Judah when he returned to his father?
answers: Reuben
Benjamin
Joseph
easy.explanation: Judah said that the boy would not be with them.

easy.question: Whose life was bound up with the boy’s life?

Judah’s
The king of Egypt’s
easy.explanation: The verse says that the father’s life was bound up with the boy’s life.

medium.question: Why was Judah afraid to return to his father without the boy?
answers: His father was deeply attached to the boy
The boy wanted to remain in Egypt
Judah had forgotten the way
medium.explanation: Judah feared that the boy’s absence would cause his father great pain.

medium.question: What does “his life is bound up with the lad’s life” mean?
answers: Their lives are deeply connected
The father is somewhere else
The father is angry and distant
medium.explanation: The phrase describes a very deep emotional bond between the father and the boy.

medium.question: What situation does Judah describe?

Judah returns to his father without the boy
The boy returns to his father while Judah remains in Egypt
medium.explanation: Judah describes returning to his father while the boy is absent.

answers: Their relationship is superficial
The father does not know the boy
Their bond is extremely deep and strong
challenge.explanation: The image of two lives being bound together expresses a powerful emotional connection.

challenge.question: Why would the boy’s absence be especially serious to his father?
answers: The father’s life was bound up with the boy’s life
The boy was king of Egypt
The boy had taken the family’s wealth
challenge.explanation: The verse explains the seriousness by describing the father’s life as bound to the boy’s.

challenge.question: What central concern does Judah present?

That his father would be devastated by the boy’s absence
That the boy would not find the road to Egypt
challenge.explanation: Judah fears the deep sorrow the boy’s absence would cause his father.

answers: Their relationship is superficial

Their bond is extremely deep and strong

answers: The father’s life was bound up with the boy’s life
The boy was king of Egypt

questions.question: What central concern does Judah present?
answers: That his father would not recognize him
That his father would be devastated by the boy’s absence
That the boy would not find the road to Egypt
questions.explanation: Judah fears the deep sorrow the boy’s absence would cause his father.

easy.question: Who would see that the boy was absent?
answers: His father
His brothers
Joseph
easy.explanation: The verse says that the father would see that the boy was not with them.

easy.question: What would happen to the father when he saw that the boy was absent?
answers: He would rejoice
He would die
He would flee
easy.explanation: The verse says that the father would die when he saw that the boy was absent.

easy.question: In what condition would Jacob’s servants bring down their father?
answers: With joy
In peace
With sorrow
easy.explanation: They would bring their father’s gray hairs down to the grave with sorrow.

medium.question: Why might the father die according to the verse?
answers: Because he would see that the boy was absent
Simply because he was old
Because his brothers had left him
medium.explanation: The verse connects the father’s death with seeing that the boy was missing.

medium.question: What does “gray hairs” indicate in this context?
answers: Youth
Old age and gray hair
A road home
medium.explanation: The expression refers to the father’s old age.

medium.question: What is the connection between the boy’s absence and the father’s sorrow?
answers: The absence would cause the father deep grief
The absence would make the father happy
The absence would not affect the father
medium.explanation: The brothers feared that their father could not survive the sorrow of losing the boy.

easy.question: Who said, “Thy servant became surety for the lad”?
answers: Judah
Joseph
Benjamin
easy.explanation: Judah was speaking and referred to himself as the ruler’s servant.

easy.question: What did Judah promise to do?
answers: Remain in Egypt
Bring the boy back to his father
Return the money
easy.explanation: Judah promised to bring the boy back to his father.

easy.question: What would happen to Judah if he did not bring back the boy?
answers: He would lose his property
He would return to Egypt
He would bear the blame to his father forever
easy.explanation: Judah said that failing to return the boy would make him guilty before his father forever.

medium.question: Why did Judah mention that he had guaranteed the boy’s safety?
answers: To show that he was the oldest brother
To ask for money
To explain why he was obligated to return the boy to his father
medium.explanation: His guarantee was the reason Judah felt responsible for bringing the boy back.

medium.question: What does “became surety for the lad” mean?
answers: He watched over him at night
He accepted responsibility for him
He hid him
medium.explanation: Judah had accepted responsibility and promised to return the boy.

medium.question: What cause-and-effect relationship appears in the verse?
answers: Because Judah guaranteed the boy’s safety, failing to return him would be Judah’s sin
Because the boy sinned, Judah became his guarantor
Because the father wanted money, Judah stayed in Egypt
medium.explanation: The guarantee created Judah’s obligation, so failing to return the boy would make him guilty.

challenge.question: What does “for ever” emphasize in Judah’s statement?
answers: The guilt would last only one day
The guilt would continue throughout his life
The guilt would be divided among the brothers
challenge.explanation: Judah says he would bear the blame continually, not just temporarily.

challenge.question: What does Judah’s use of “thy servant” show about how he addresses the ruler?
answers: He speaks respectfully and humbly
He treats the ruler as his younger brother
He claims equal status with the ruler
challenge.explanation: The expression is respectful and shows Judah’s humility before the ruler.

challenge.question: Who is meant by “unto thee” in “If I bring him not unto thee”?
answers: Judah’s father
The boy
The person Judah is addressing
challenge.explanation: The phrase addresses the ruler directly.

easy.question: Who offered to remain a slave instead of the boy?
answers: Judah
Benjamin
One of the other brothers
easy.explanation: Judah offered to remain as a slave in the boy’s place.

easy.question: Who was supposed to go up with his brothers?
answers: Judah
The boy
The master
easy.explanation: The verse says that the boy should go up with his brothers.

easy.question: What did Judah offer to do so that the boy could leave?
answers: Return the boy to his father
Remain as a slave to the ruler
Send all the brothers to prison
easy.explanation: Judah offered to remain as the ruler’s slave so that the boy could go with his brothers.

medium.question: Why did Judah offer to remain instead of the boy?
answers: So the boy could go up with his brothers
To receive payment
To separate himself from his brothers
medium.explanation: Judah wanted to take the boy’s place so that the boy could return with the others.

medium.question: What does “instead of the lad” mean in context?
answers: Above the boy
In the boy’s place
Beside the boy
medium.explanation: Judah asked to remain as a slave in the boy’s place.

medium.question: What sequence of actions does Judah propose?
answers: The boy will remain, and the brothers will leave
The ruler will remain, and the boy will flee
Judah will remain a slave, and the boy will go up with his brothers
medium.explanation: Judah first offers himself as a slave and then says the boy can leave with his brothers.

challenge.question: What does Judah’s use of “thy servant” show about his attitude toward the ruler?
answers: He speaks respectfully and accepts the ruler’s authority
He claims to be the ruler’s equal
He accuses the ruler of deception
challenge.explanation: Calling himself the ruler’s servant expresses humility and respect.

challenge.question: What change in roles does Judah propose?
answers: The ruler becomes a slave and the boy becomes a master
Judah remains a slave in the boy’s place, and the boy is freed
All the brothers become slaves instead of Judah
challenge.explanation: Judah offers to exchange places with the boy.

challenge.question: What does “and let the lad go up with his brethren” emphasize?
answers: The boy is Judah’s oldest brother
The boy is unrelated to the proposal
Judah’s offer is meant to allow the boy to leave with his brothers
challenge.explanation: The boy’s freedom is the purpose of Judah’s offer.

answers: Go up to his father
Find the boy
Return to Egypt
easy.explanation: Judah asks how he can go up to his father without the boy.

easy.question: Who would not be with Judah?
answers: His father
The boy
His brothers

easy.question: What did Judah fear would happen to his father?

His father would leave his home
His father would suffer evil
easy.explanation: Judah feared seeing the evil that would come upon his father.

medium.question: Why could Judah not go up to his father?
answers: The boy would not be with him
He did not know the way
His father was not at home
medium.explanation: The boy’s absence made Judah unable to return to his father.

medium.question: What does “lest” express in “lest peradventure I see the evil”?
answers: Certainty
Fear that something might happen
A conclusion
medium.explanation: Judah feared that he might see the harm that would come to his father.

medium.question: What might happen if Judah returned to his father without the boy?
answers: His father would send him away again
The boy would arrive alone
Judah would see the evil that would come upon his father
medium.explanation: Judah connects returning without the boy with disaster for his father.

challenge.question: What does “How shall I go up to my father?” express beyond a question about travel?
answers: Distress and a moral inability to return without the boy
A desire to know which road to take
Joy at seeing his father
challenge.explanation: It is a rhetorical question expressing Judah’s anguish and sense of responsibility.

answers: The boy is already with the father
Judah feels responsible for bringing the boy back with him
The boy does not know the way
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes Judah’s responsibility to return with the boy.

answers: The boy
The father
The evil that may come upon the father
